{{Codex|A living weapon, the infested Embolist pistol kills its victims with an acidic venomous gas.}}

The '''Embolist''' fires a toxic stream of poison with a high chance to proc {{D|Toxin}}.

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals only {{D|Toxin}} damage.
*Damage ramps up from 45% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 45% over 2 seconds.
*The zone of impact or maximum beam range produces a spherical blast radius of '''1''' meter, allowing it to hit multiple enemies at once.
**The radial damage is not affected by multishot.
**The radius is affected by ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}) {{M|Fulmination}}.
*{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon.
*Can use the Embolist-exclusive mods {{M|Eroding Blight}} and {{M|Vile Discharge}}.
*Innate {{Pol|Naramon}} polarity.

{{Advantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held|
*Pinpoint [[accuracy]].
*Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage.
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held|
*Limited range of '''9''' meters.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Embolist's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Bio Lab|Bio Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*The projectile creates a toxin cloud on whatever surface it hits, this is purely cosmetic and does no additional damage, staying for less than a second.

==Tips==
*As the Embolist is primarily a close range weapon that benefits from area of effect, {{M|Magnum Force}} can be beneficial in increasing both its damage and its spread.
*{{M|Ruinous Extension}} will increase the range of the weapon by almost double (from a max range of 9m to 17m).
*Multishot affects the beam but not the small radial damage effect where the beam ends.
*Punch Through can be slotted but has no effect on the weapon.

==Trivia==
*An [[wikipedia:embolism|embolism]] refers to the lodging of an [[wikipedia:embolus|embolus]], such as a blood clot or gas bubble. It can cause a circulatory blockage which affects a different part of the body away from the actual site of the blockage.
*The visual effect of the Embolist resembles the special attack of the [[Nauseous Crawler]], indicating that this weapon may be a part of said Infested or derived from it. However, apart from the similar attack appearance there are no shared properties.
*The 'tail' on this weapon moves.
*Interestingly, the weapon's reload animation seems to involve pulling (or possibly twisting) the weapon's tail.
*Originally the weapon behaved exactly like the [[Ignis]], having infinite body punch through and having the rare effect of proccing toxin on every hit even if the weapon's toxin was changed to a new element. Both of these mechanics were entirely removed for unknown reasons.

==Known Bugs==
*When given to a [[Rescue|Rescue target]], the cloud released when fired will be the Embolist's default energy color, as opposed to the customized one shown on the weapon itself.
*{{M|Galvanized Shot}} is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from alt-fire if using {{M|Vile Discharge}}.

{{Codex|Brain-strikes excite this bioweapon, causing it to rapidly release toxic munitions.}}

The '''Dual Toxocyst''' is a pair of {{Faction|Infested}} sidearms oriented towards {{D|Puncture}} damage. Successfully achieving a headshot with this weapon temporarily grants it increased [[fire rate]], additional {{D|Toxin}} damage, reduced [[recoil]] and [[Ammo Efficiency|infinite ammo]]. However, its initial recoil is very high and initial fire rate is very slow.

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Landing a successful headshot grants the '''Frenzy''' buff.
**Frenzy buffs lasts for '''3''' seconds, and can be refreshed on subsequent headshots.
**Frenzy grants the following buffs: 
***'''+150%''' [[Fire Rate]]
****Bonus is multiplicative to other sources of fire rate.
***'''+100%''' [[Ammo Efficiency]]
***'''-75%''' [[Recoil]]
***'''+100%''' {{D|Toxin}} damage
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} and {{Pol|Naramon}} polarities.

{{Advantages|
*Very good ammo efficiency.
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*High recoil without the innate buff active.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Dual Toxocyst's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Bio Lab|Bio Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*Frenzy buff triggers '''only''' on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]], and not other weakspots, such as the backpacks of most [[MOA]] variants. Similarly, shooting weakspots generated by either {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}} in places other than heads will have no effect either.
**Headshots on corpses will not grant the buff.
*The fire rate bonus from Frenzy stacks multiplicatively after any equipped fire rate mods or fire rate bonuses.
*The +100% {{D|Toxin}} from Frenzy is additive with elemental mods, and will combine with elemental mods equipped on the weapon, ex. having {{M|Heated Charge}} or {{M|Scorch|Scorch}} equipped will make the Dual Toxocyst deal {{D|Gas}} upon activating the buff.
**If the Dual Toxocyst is modded with a combined element such as {{D|Corrosive}}, the bonus toxin damage will be added to that element's damage.
*If Frenzy is triggered or if it disappears, this weapon makes a noise that will alert nearby enemies. This noise '''cannot''' be reduced with {{M|Suppress}} or {{M|Hushed Invisibility}}.
*Triggering the buff with the last bullet of the magazine does not require the user to reload the weapon before shooting again because it stops consuming ammo, and therefore is an effective candidate for {{M|Synth Charge}}.

==Incarnon Genesis==
{{Transclude|Dual Toxocyst Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}}

{{Transclude|Dual Toxocyst Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}}

==Tips==
*The headshot buff can completely counter the weapon's low innate fire rate and max ammo capacity.
*If modded with {{D|Gas}}, the gas clouds deals a tick of damage each second, each tick has a chance to refresh the "'''Frenzy'''" buff.
*Zoom bonuses (i.e. {{M|Hawk Eye}}) can make gaining the headshot buff easier, significantly increasing the weapon's damage output and versatility.
*The {{Weapon|Scourge}} synergizes well with these pistols as the speargun can debuff enemies with {{A|Magnetize}}-like fields on their heads when thrown and left to allow it to recast its debuff at fixed intervals.
*The added {{D|Toxin}} damage when landing headshots makes the pistols deceptively effective against any shielded {{Faction|Corpus}} enemies.
*While under the effects of the triggered buff, the fast fire rate and unlimited ammo, combined with the low [[critical chance]] and average critical multiplier make rapid fire bodyshots more viable than aimed headshots.
*{{M|Hydraulic Crosshairs}} can be triggered at the same time as the buff, though the low base [[critical chance]] makes this mod of limited utility without the Commodore's Fortune evolution of its Incarnon.
*Installing {{M|Steady Hands}} completely negates recoil while buff is active.

==Trivia==
*The Dual Toxocyst is the first infested dual pistol added to the game.
*Triggering the innate headshot buff or reloading the weapon will cause the Dual Toxocyst's barrel to open up like jaws, connected by infested tissue between its upper and lower parts.

Charge the shot to fire a punishing high-velocity, high critical chance slab that punches through barriers. Deals additional headshot damage in Sevagoth's hands.}} The '''Epitaph''' is {{WF|Sevagoth}}'s [[Signature Weapon|signature]] wrist-mounted sidearm. Uncharged shots fire explosive slabs with extreme [[status chance]] and a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc, while fully charged shots possess extreme [[critical chance]] and [[critical multiplier]] with [[punch through]]. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals pure {{D|Blast}} damage uncharged and primarily {{D|Slash}} damage fully charged. *Shots have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc on direct hits. *Uncharged shots: **Tied with {{Weapon|Epitaph Prime}}, {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}} and {{Weapon|Tysis}} for the highest [[status chance]] of all secondaries. **Explodes in an '''8''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy. ***Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. ***Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. ***Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}). **Have a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc. *Charged shots: **Second highest [[critical chance]] of all secondaries, behind {{Weapon|Epitaph Prime}}. **High [[critical multiplier]]. **Very fast charge speed. **Innate 2 meter [[punch through]]. *Deals '''+20%''' [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] damage when wielded by {{WF|Sevagoth}}/{{WF|Sevagoth Prime}}. *{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. *Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. {{Advantages| *No magazine; does not need to reload. }} {{Disadvantages| *Uncharged Shots: **Lowest critical multiplier of all secondaries. **Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. **Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. **Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 20% from central impact. *Projectiles have travel time. Uncharged shots have slower projectile speed with heavy arcing. }} {{WeaponComparison|Epitaph Prime}} *Uncharged Shot: **Lower base damage (20.00 vs. 30.00) **Lower base critical chance (2.00% vs. 4.00%) **Lower base critical multiplier (1.20x vs 1.80x) **Lower range (8m vs. 10m) ==Acquisition== This weapon's blueprint and components can be acquired from [[Void Storm]] missions in [[Earth Proxima]], [[Venus Proxima]], and [[Saturn Proxima]]. All parts can be [[Trading|traded]] between players. {{Acquisition|name=Epitaph|header=n}} {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Sevagoth's [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] bonus only applies to actual heads and not any other weak spot. *Epitaph draws ammo directly from the full ammo pool similar to bows, but does not "reload" between shots like them. The delay between shots is all based on its 1.5 fire-rate (0.67s), and Epitaph's displayed 0.6s reload time has no purpose. *A [[Specter]] with the Epitaph equipped will only use its Uncharged Shot. ==Tips== *Because of both its low fire rate and guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc on direct hits, the Epitaph is a perfect candidate for {{M|Hemorrhage}} to nearly guarantee {{D|Slash}} procs on every hit. *Epitaph's ability to inflict guaranteed {{D|Cold}} status makes it a self-sufficient user of {{Arcane|Secondary Shiver}}. Epitaph is also one of a select few weapons for which Secondary Shiver and other [[GunCO]] effects are multiplicative with base damage mods, instead of adding to them, making for an even stronger damage boost than usual on direct hits. ==Trivia== *An '''[[wikipedia:Epitaph|epitaph]]''' is a phrase honoring a deceased person, commonly written on tombstones. ==Known Bugs== *When {{M|Suppress}} is installed, enemies will still react to the weapon being fired, and eventually get alerted, making it bad for stealth gameplay. *{{M|Galvanized Shot}} and other [[GunCO]] effects are multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits in both firing modes. **For charged shots bonus is multiplied by charge bonus (2x). ==Media== File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-screenshot055.jpg File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-screenshot056.jpg File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-screenshot052.jpg|Without the slab File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-screenshot053.jpg File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-screenshot054.jpg File:Tim-bergholz-chamferzone-com-highpolysidearm.jpg File:EpitaphConcept.PNG|Concept art File:EpitaphConcept1.png File:EpitaphConcept2.png File:EpitaphConcept3.png {{YouTube|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yswNykYwVmw}} {{YouTube|TMtsO1-ttCA}} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|39.0.7}} *Fixed floating rope pieces floating on the Epitaph Raya Skin. {{ver|37}} *Reduced the audio gain on Epitaph Prime’s projectile and explosion. {{ver|35.0.7}} *Fixed dual wielding with the Cirriped Epitaph Skin equipped causing the Epitaph to have offset issues. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 20 Ammo per Pick Up: *Epitaph '''Many weapons have also had their maximum ammo capacity adjusted.''' Secondary Weapons: *Epitaph: From 60 to 40 ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|30.3.1}} *Fixed the Epitaph moving around and being in random positions when swapping back and forth between Primary and Secondary weapons several times, when getting staggered or when throwing a Glaive while Dual Wielding. {{ver|30.3}} *Fixed arm cannon type (Epitaph) reticle area being blocked by a part of Zephyr Harrier's shoulder element. {{ver|30.0.8}} *Fixed Wisp not raising her arm when firing the Epitaph. {{ver|30.0.7}} *The Epitaph Blueprint is now tradeable. *Added updated wrist-mounted weapon animations (i.e. Epitaph). **Also fixes weird wrist angled animations. {{ver|30.0.6}} *Fixed ability to equip the Synth Charge Mod to Epitaph. **Epitaph does not meet the magazine size requirement for Synth Charge. {{ver|30}} *Introduced. }} {{WeaponNav}} [[es:Epitaph]] [[ru:Эпитаф]] [[fr:Épitaphe]] [[Category:Slow]] [[Category:Update 30]] [[Category:Sevagoth]] [[Category:Signature Weapons]] [[uk:Епітафія]]

{{Codex|Send shivers down your enemies' spines with this wrist-mounted sidearm. As the signature weapon of Sevagoth Prime, it deals additional headshot damage when wielded by him.}}
'''Epitaph Prime''' is the [[Prime]]d counterpart of {{Weapon|Epitaph}} wrist-mounted sidearm, with slight improvements to its damage and already high [[critical chance]] and [[critical multiplier]], charged shot's [[status chance]], and uncharged shot's [[fire rate]] and explosion radius. Additionally, charged shots have a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} status proc. Epitaph Prime was released alongside {{WF|Sevagoth Prime}} and {{Companion|Nautilus Prime}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals pure {{D|Blast}} damage uncharged and primarily {{D|Slash}} damage fully charged.
*Shots have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc on direct hits.
*Uncharged shots:
**Tied with {{Weapon|Epitaph}}, {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}} and {{Weapon|Tysis}} for the highest [[status chance]] of all secondaries.
**Explodes in a '''10''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy.
***Initial hit and explosion apply status separately.
***Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
***Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}).
***Has a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc.
*Charged shots:
**Highest [[critical chance]] of all secondaries.
**High [[critical multiplier]].
**Very fast charge speed.
**Innate 2 meter [[punch through]].
**Has a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc.
*Deals '''+20%''' [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] damage when wielded by {{WF|Sevagoth}}/{{WF|Sevagoth Prime}}.
*{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon.
*Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities.

{{Advantages|
*No magazine; does not need to reload.
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Uncharged Shots:
**Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]].

'''Dual Coda Torxica''' are unique [[Coda]] dual pistols that tags enemies to release {{D|Cold}} spores upon their death, applying [[Damage Vulnerability]].

==Characteristics==
*This weapon primarily deals {{D|Slash}} damage.
*Enemies killed by the Dual Coda Torxica will spread spores to '''3''' enemies within '''20''' meters with the closest being prioritized, inflicting guaranteed {{D|Cold}} status per second and '''50%''' [[Damage Vulnerability]] lasting for '''20''' seconds. 
**Damage Vulnerability only applies to damage inflicted by the Dual Coda Torxica, not any other source.
*Adversary Weapon:
**Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%.
***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%).
**[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity.
**{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely.
**Unlike [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] and [[Tenet]] weapons directly acquired from a [[Kuva Lich]] or [[Sisters of Parvos]], the listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement '''is''' enforced.

{{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Coda Acquisition}}

==Notes==
*When an enemy is killed by the Dual Coda Torxica, they spread '''3''' spores to nearby enemies within '''20''' meters. Enemies affected by spores will suffer '''50%''' [[Damage Vulnerability]] for '''20''' seconds, while also suffering from a guaranteed {{D|Cold}} proc each second.
**Spores are created by kills from status damage, as well as from direct damage. 
**Spores will prioritize enemies closest to the target, and enemies can only suffer from '''1''' spore at a time.
***Affected enemies will glow based on the location the spore hit them, which serves purely as a visual indicator and has no effect on damage received (unlike similar indicators from {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}}). 
**Spores can properly debuff {{E|Arbitration Shield Drone}}s and tethered enemies, the drones will become vulnerable to damage and show hits of {{D|Cold}} procs with no damage number.
**{{D|Cold}} procs can build up over time, but as they use the standard 6-second [[Status Duration]], which can be modified if the player desires, affected enemies can only suffer up to 6 Cold procs at a time before the earliest proc expires. The spores' duration cannot be changed.
**Spores will '''only''' inflict {{D|Cold}} procs, which deal no additional damage and cannot have additional status effects forced upon them via [[Abilities]].
***{{Arcane|Secondary Encumber}} is an exception to this, as spore procs can trigger this Arcane and, assuming a fully-ranked Arcane, generate one additional status effect on average.
***Spores cannot trigger {{Arcane|Cascadia Empowered}}.
**The damage vulnerability behaves like a faction damage mod as it is applied '''twice''' to status effects. It is however a unique modifier and multiplicative to faction damage mods or other damage vulnerability sources.  
*The Dual Coda Torxica sports a unique reticle that changes when the player is aiming at a target affected by spores, gaining 3 asymmetrical growths.
*Spores will amplify damage of ANY Dual Coda Torxica should any other entity other than spore source wield the weapon. This includes party members, operatives, specters and summons (granted you equip them with Dual Coda Torxica)
*Non-player entities can not spread spores by killing with Dual Coda Torxica. However, spores will spread if enemy was damaged by player's Dual Coda Torxica and was killed by non-player entity with Dual Coda Torxica damage (as this satisfies the conditions of 'damaged and killed by Dual Coda Torxica'). Spores created this way will belong to the damaging player. 
{{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}}

==Tips==
*Spores can be spread through obstacles, which can help locate enemies through walls.
*Security cameras and turrets can be affected by spores.

==Trivia==
*On [[Devstream 184]], the weapon was named '''Dual Coda Nicardia'''.
*Instead of using the same prefix arrangement as other akimbo weapons like {{Weapon|Kuva Twin Stubbas}} and {{Weapon|Prisma Twin Gremlins}} with variant prefix (Kuva/Prisma/Coda) before akimbo prefix (Twin/Dual) as ''Coda Dual'' Torxica, Dual Coda Torxica goes the other way around with akimbo prefix before variant prefix.
*The Dual Coda Torxica's reload, like all Coda weapons, has a unique animation. This one is designed around the Torxica's mutated handles, where the Warframe feeds the guns by tossing two small glowing sacks into its mouths.
*Torx (which the weapon might derive its name from) is a brand of screw drive characterized by a 6-point star-shaped pattern. This appears to be alluding to the weapons being Infested power drills.
*While firing, the Dual Coda Torxica makes the sound of a drill spinning. This is most noticeable after the player stops firing, as you can hear the drills coming to a stop. This sound can still be heard regardless of weapon skins.
*The Infested barrels of the Dual Coda Torxica spins up while they are firing, and then slow to a stop when firing stops. The rate at which they spin is affected by the fire rate.

{{Codex|Turn the enemy's worst nightmare into reality with Follie's signature rifle. The Enkaus will instantly kill and dissolve inked enemies that are damaged at low health. Shooting inked enemies siphons ink back into the Enkaus, allowing for a constant flow of creative destruction.}}
'''Enkaus''' is {{WF|Follie}}'s [[Signature Weapon|signature]] [[Continuous Weapon|beam]] rifle, hosing down its targets with a stream of {{D|Corrosive}} ink. Its [[Alternate Fire]] launches a glob of ink that stains enemies, allowing follow-up primary fire to refund Enkaus ammo and instantly dissolving them when they hit a certain health threshold.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon primarily deals {{D|Corrosive}} damage.
*This weapon does not use ammo pickups, instead having infinite reserve ammo.
*[[Alternate Fire]] consumes '''15''' ammo to launch an ink projectile that explodes in an '''8''' meter radius on contact with enemies or a surface. Enemies hit by the blast are covered with ink for '''20''' seconds. The projectile will also leave a puddle with a '''8''' meter radius, lasting for '''10''' seconds and staining enemies that come into contact with it.
**When wielded by {{WF|Follie}}, the [[Alternate Fire]] applies [[Follie/Abilities/Passive|Inkblot]], Follie's passive.
***Enemies afflicted by Inkblot are considered ink-stained targets, even if the Enkaus's alternate fire wasn't used.
**Shooting ink-stained enemies with the primary fire draws ink back into the weapon, causing the Enkaus to consume no ammo and restore '''0.33''' ammo per hit for each enemy hit.
**{{M|Firestorm}} increases the area of the paint left on the ground.
**Ink-stained enemies will be dissolved and instantly killed if Enkaus drops their health below '''35%'''. Enemy health can be lowered by other sources before instakilling them with Enkaus.
***Enemies with special states such as {{E|Thrax Centurion}} or {{E|Kuva Larvling}} will not be dissolved to avoid breaking their mechanics. Bosses cannot be instakilled.
***AoE extra-hit sources (e.g. {{M|Combustion Beam}}, {{D|Blast}} procs) will trigger the instakill.
***When wielded by {{WF|Garuda}}, while the enemy is inflicted with {{A|Seeking Talons}}, the instakill damage element will change from {{D|Corrosive}} to {{D|Slash}}.
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity.
